road.title: Time and days
road.place: The Polite Dell of the Short Straw
road.description: A round and unhurried shape wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Fergus is a Clockwinder to the District and winds every clock in town by hand and is, as a result, always a little behind.

character.name: Fergus Lintel
character.description: A round and unhurried shape wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Fergus is a Clockwinder to the District and winds every clock in town by hand and is, as a result, always a little behind.

npc.narrative: This mattina the pioggia comes down hard, and il fulmine lights the piazza like an inspection. Fergus Lintel stands sotto the grande clock tower, a key in his mano, winding with perfect calma. Every orologio above him is wrong in its own way.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Sono Fergus. Io non so mai che ore sono. Tu hai un orologio?
npc.translation: Good morning! I am Fergus. I never know what time it is. Do you have a clock?

player: Buongiorno Fergus. No, non ho orologio. Che ore sono?

correction.text: Buongiorno Fergus. No, non ho l'orologio. Che ore sono?
correction.translation: Good morning Fergus. No, I don't have a watch. What time is it?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Fergus, answered his question and asked him the time in Italian. Just remember the little word \"l'\" before \"orologio\".

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked Fergus what time it is with "Che ore sono?".
You didn't ask Fergus what day it is today yet; we'll come back to it later, so try asking him about the day.
You didn't ask Fergus at what time something opens, starts or leaves yet; we'll ask for this again later.

correction.text: Buongiorno Fergus. No, non ho l'orologio. Che ore sono?
correction.translation: Good morning Fergus. No, I don't have a watch. What time is it?

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Fergus what day it is today, using Italian.
Ask Fergus at what time it opens, starts or leaves, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Sotto the grande ombrello of the torre, Fergus winds a vecchio clock while the pioggia drums and a fulmine makes the dial briefly accurate. He nods at you, unhurried, with a chiave in one hand. He is ancora a little behind.
npc.native: Bravo! Io non so l'ora. Non so nemmeno che giorno è oggi. Tu lo sai?
npc.translation: Well done! I do not know the time. I do not even know what day it is today. Do you know?

player: No, non lo so. Oggi è lunedì? Non so.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice try. Your Italian sentences were clear, and you said you didn't know and made a guess about the day. Next, try turning the question around and asking Fergus.

objectiveResults.feedback: You answered Fergus's question, but the goal here is to ask him what day it is today, so we'll try that again.
Here you'd ask Fergus at what time something opens, starts or leaves. We'll come back to this one later.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Fergus what day it is today, using Italian.
Ask Fergus at what time it opens, starts or leaves, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The pioggia hammers the tetto of the torre, and every lampo turns the dials briefly white. Fergus stands on a scala with a piccolo oilcan, winding one orologio while the next falls behind. He nods at you as if the tempesta were a late customer, and the mattina carries on regardless.
npc.native: Forse è lunedì, bravo! Ogni mattina chiedo «che giorno è» e nessuno risponde. Tu hai un calendario?
npc.translation: Maybe it is Monday, well done! Every morning I ask "what day is it" and nobody answers. Do you have a calendar?

player: No calendario. Che giorno è oggi? E a che ora apre il bar?

correction.text: Non ho il calendario. Che giorno è oggi? E a che ora apre il bar?
correction.translation: I don't have a calendar. What day is it today? And at what time does the bar open?

verdict.overallFeedback: You answered Fergus about the calendar and then asked him two clear questions, one about the day and one about when the bar opens. Just one small fix: say \"Non ho il calendario\" for \"I don't have a calendar\".

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you asked Fergus what day it is with "Che giorno è oggi?".
Well done, you asked at what time the bar opens with "a che ora apre il bar?".

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: a che ora apre il bar?

correction.text: Non ho il calendario. Che giorno è oggi? E a che ora apre il bar?
correction.translation: I don't have a calendar. What day is it today? And at what time does the bar open?

npc.narrative: La pioggia drums on the tetto of the shed, and a lampo turns every quadrante white for a moment. Fergus stands on a scala with a grande chiave, già eleven minutes behind and perfectly calm. He consults the guild rulebook, which has nothing on bars, e nods anyway.
npc.native: Bravo, due domande! Oggi è lunedì, credo. Il bar apre alle nove. A che ora arrivi tu?
npc.translation: Well done, two questions! Today is Monday, I think. The bar opens at nine. At what time do you arrive?

player: Arrivo alle nove. Tu vieni al bar?

npc.narrative: Il tuono rolls over the piazza, and the pioggia comes down in hard grey rods. Fergus stands under an awning with a scala, a chiave the size of a spoon, and an orologio that has stopped, which is within its rights. He consults his own watch, which has a different opinion.
npc.native: Sì, vengo al bar, ma arrivo tardi. Gli orologi aspettano. Tu prendi un caffè?
npc.translation: Yes, I come to the bar, but I arrive late. The clocks are waiting. Do you have a coffee?

player: Si, un caffè. Ciao Fergus, a dopo!

npc.narrative: Il temporale sits on the tetto like a tenant who owes rent, and la pioggia comes down in sheets. Fergus consults his orologio, which is un po' indietro. A tuono rolls past, unhurried, with a form to file.
npc.native: Un caffè, bene! Fuori c'è un temporale. Prendi anche un cornetto?
npc.translation: A coffee, good! Outside there is a storm. Do you also have a croissant?
